newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police seize stolen gold concentrate.
newsitem.headline: S.African police seize stolen gold concentrate.

text.p: Around 20 kg (44 pounds) of gold concentrate was seized after three suspects were arrested in connection with the theft from South Africa's Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd on Thursday, police said.

Police spokeswoman Rulene Kuhn said security guards spotted six men running away from Harmony's Merriespruit plant before dawn. A guard shot and wounded one of the suspects in the leg. Two others were arrested later.

"Eight bags of gold dust was seized," Kuhn said in a statement. Police were unable to quantify the gold's value but a Harmony metallurgical official said the bags contained about 20 kg of gold concentrate that had not been assayed.
Harmony's security team also arrested five men in possession of 220 kg (484 pounds) of gold concentrate outside the plant at Merriespruit on Sunday.
Harmony Managing Director Bernard Swanepoel warned in a statement after the arrests that the company would take a tough line on gold theft.

"Theft is a major problem in the industry, which we are determined to stamp out," Swanepoel said. "We intend to increase security and will not hesitate to prosecute individuals caught stealing from the mine."
South Africa is the world's biggest gold-producing country, producing 522.4 tonnes in 1994, or 23 percent of global output.
